```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(targets)

violations <- tar_read(violations)
numeric_summary <- tar_read(numeric_summary_all)
level_summary <- tar_read(level_summary_all)
invariant_checks <- tar_read(invariant_check_all)
grain <- tar_read(grain_all)
manifest <- tar_read(data_manifest)
schema <- tar_read(dataschema)
exposures <- tar_read(exposure_registry)

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
id_order <- function(x) factor(x, levels = unique(x[order(as.numeric(x))]))
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 9))
```

A permanent QA tool, rebuilt whenever a dataset changes.
Nothing here is a pipeline failure: each finding is something to look at, and ends in a harmonisation fix, an analysis exception or no action.
Data: `r nrow(manifest)` datasets, overall hash `r unique(manifest$overall_hash)`.

## Findings by check

```{r}
#| label: findings-summary
check_labels <- c(
  above_max = "Numeric value above the schema maximum",
  below_min = "Numeric value below the schema minimum",
  outside_allowed_values = "Level not in the schema's allowed values (advisory)",
  screen_constant = "Screen-time variable with one distinct value in a wave",
  screen_all_zero = "Screen-time variable all zero in a wave",
  screen_scale = "Screen-time variable far from other datasets (possible unit error)",
  usual_day_outside_week = "Usual-day mean outside the weekday and weekend means",
  invariant_varies = "Carried row takes more than one value within a participant",
  duplicate_key = "More than one row per participant, wave and measure",
  missing_participant_id = "Rows with no participant ID"
)
violations |>
  summarise(
    datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id),
    variables = n_distinct(variable_name, na.rm = TRUE),
    findings = n(),
    affected = sum(n),
    .by = c(check, severity)
  ) |>
  mutate(Check = coalesce(check_labels[check], check)) |>
  arrange(severity, desc(findings)) |>
  transmute(Check, Severity = severity, Datasets = datasets, Variables = variables, Findings = findings, `Cells or participants` = fmt(affected)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrr")
```

## Findings by dataset

```{r}
#| label: findings-by-dataset
violations |>
  filter(severity == "review") |>
  count(dataset_id, check) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = check, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(as.numeric(dataset_id)) |>
  rename(Dataset = dataset_id) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Findings to review, per dataset. Datasets with none are not listed.")
```

`r nrow(manifest) - n_distinct(violations$dataset_id[violations$severity == "review"])` of `r nrow(manifest)` datasets have no finding to review.

## Values outside the schema's bounds

The harmonisation guide keeps out-of-range scores for the analysis to screen, so these are expected in small numbers.
A large share in one dataset usually means a different score form or a mapping error.

```{r}
#| label: bounds
violations |>
  filter(check %in% c("above_max", "below_min")) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), denominator = sum(denominator), waves = n(), detail = first(detail), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name, check)) |>
  mutate(share = n / denominator) |>
  arrange(desc(share)) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, Check = check, Cells = fmt(n), Share = pct(share), Waves = waves, Example = detail) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllrrrl")
```

## Screen time

### Location and spread across datasets

Each line is one dataset's 5th to 95th percentile, with its quartiles and median, pooled over its waves on the primary measure.
A dataset far to the right of the others may be in minutes.

```{r}
#| label: screen-fn
hours_vars <- exposures$variable_name[exposures$unit %in% "hours"]
dataset_quantiles <- function(vars) {
  numeric_summary |>
    filter(variable_name %in% vars, st_measure_id == "primary") |>
    summarise(
      across(c(p05, p25, median, p75, p95), \(x) weighted.mean(x, n)),
      n = sum(n),
      .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name)
    )
}
quantile_plot <- function(vars, ncol = 3) {
  d <- dataset_quantiles(vars)
  if (nrow(d) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  ggplot(d, aes(y = id_order(dataset_id))) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = p05, xmax = p95), colour = "grey60") +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = p25, xmax = p75), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(aes(x = median), colour = "firebrick", size = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(vars(variable_name), scales = "free", ncol = ncol) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Dataset") +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-screen-main
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 16
quantile_plot(c("st_total", "st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational", "st_comp", "st_tablet", "st_phone", "st_internet"))
```

```{r}
#| label: screen-high
numeric_summary |>
  filter(variable_name %in% hours_vars, st_measure_id == "primary") |>
  summarise(p95 = weighted.mean(p95, n), max = max(max), n = sum(n), .by = c(dataset_id, variable_name)) |>
  filter(p95 >= 10) |>
  arrange(desc(p95)) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, N = fmt(n), `95th percentile (hours)` = signif(p95, 3), Maximum = signif(max, 3)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "Dataset and variable pairs whose 95th percentile is 10 hours a day or more.")
```

### Scale, constant and usual-day findings

```{r}
#| label: screen-findings
violations |>
  filter(check %in% c("screen_scale", "screen_constant", "screen_all_zero", "usual_day_outside_week")) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, Wave = wave, Measure = st_measure_id, Check = check, N = fmt(n), Detail = detail) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lllllrl")
```

### Response bands and declared measure type

The number of distinct values a dataset records, against what `st_measure_type` says.
A "Continuous" measure with a handful of distinct values, or a banded one with many, deserves a look.

```{r}
#| label: measure-type
measure_type <- level_summary |>
  filter(variable_name == "st_measure_type", level != "Unknown") |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(dataset_id, st_measure_id)) |>
  select(dataset_id, st_measure_id, measure_type = level)
distinct_values <- numeric_summary |>
  filter(variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational", "st_total")) |>
  summarise(distinct = max(n_distinct), n = sum(n), .by = c(dataset_id, st_measure_id, variable_name)) |>
  left_join(measure_type, by = c("dataset_id", "st_measure_id"))
distinct_values |>
  mutate(band = cut(distinct, c(0, 4, 8, 15, 30, Inf), labels = c("1-4", "5-8", "9-15", "16-30", "31+"))) |>
  count(measure_type, band) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = band, values_from = n, values_fill = 0, names_sort = TRUE) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dataset, measure and variable combinations by declared type and number of distinct values.")
```

## Carried rows

```{r}
#| label: invariants
invariant_checks |>
  summarise(
    datasets = n(),
    datasets_varying = sum(participants_varying > 0),
    repeated = sum(participants_repeated),
    varying = sum(participants_varying),
    .by = variable_name
  ) |>
  mutate(share = varying / pmax(repeated, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(varying)) |>
  transmute(Variable = variable_name, Datasets = datasets, `Datasets where it varies` = datasets_varying, `Participants seen twice or more` = fmt(repeated), `Participants with more than one value` = fmt(varying), Share = pct(share)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: invariants-detail
invariant_checks |>
  filter(participants_varying > 0) |>
  mutate(share = participants_varying / pmax(participants_repeated, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(share)) |>
  head(40) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset_id, Variable = variable_name, `Seen twice or more` = fmt(participants_repeated), Varying = fmt(participants_varying), Share = pct(share)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "The 40 dataset and variable pairs where a carried row varies most.")
```

## Grain

```{r}
#| label: grain
grain |>
  summarise(rows = sum(rows), participants = sum(participants), duplicate_keys = sum(duplicate_keys), missing_ids = sum(missing_ids), datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = st_measure_id) |>
  transmute(Measure = st_measure_id, Datasets = datasets, Rows = fmt(rows), `Participant-waves` = fmt(participants), `Duplicate keys` = fmt(duplicate_keys), `Rows with no ID` = fmt(missing_ids)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrrr")
```

## Categorical variables against the schema

Advisory until `allowed_values` is maintained.

```{r}
#| label: allowed
violations |>
  filter(check == "outside_allowed_values") |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), cells = sum(n), .by = c(variable_name, detail)) |>
  arrange(desc(cells)) |>
  head(60) |>
  transmute(Variable = variable_name, Level = detail, Datasets = datasets, Cells = fmt(cells)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrr", caption = "The 60 unlisted levels with most cells.")
```

## Continuous outcomes across datasets

One panel per variable with data in two or more datasets: each dataset's 5th to 95th percentile, quartiles and median.
Instruments differ between datasets on generic rows, so different locations are expected there; on instrument-specific rows they are not.

```{r}
#| label: outcome-panels
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 12
outcome_domains <- c("academic", "behaviour", "cognition", "mental_health", "wellbeing", "health", "family")
numeric_vars <- schema |>
  filter(domain %in% outcome_domains, data_type == "double") |>
  select(variable_name, domain)
with_data <- numeric_summary |>
  filter(st_measure_id == "primary") |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = variable_name) |>
  filter(datasets >= 2) |>
  inner_join(numeric_vars, by = "variable_name")
for (domain_name in outcome_domains) {
  vars <- sort(with_data$variable_name[with_data$domain == domain_name])
  if (length(vars) == 0) next
  cat("\n\n### ", domain_name, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (chunk in split(vars, ceiling(seq_along(vars) / 12))) {
    print(quantile_plot(chunk, ncol = 4))
    cat("\n\n")
  }
}
```
